name: Should I choose a drop beam or a flush-mounted beam when opening a wall?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a drop beam or a flush-mounted beam when opening a wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: When removing a load-bearing wall, you can choose between a drop beam or a flush hidden beam. A drop beam sits directly beneath your existing ceiling joists. It is less labor-intensive to install, which keeps remodeling labor costs down, but it leaves a visible soffit or trimmed header dividing the ceiling. A flush beam is recessed directly into the ceiling joist cavity, creating a continuous, flat ceiling plane across rooms. The tradeoff is increased labor, as every intersecting joist must be cut back and individually hung from the beam using metal joist hangers.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drop beams sit below joists and cost less to install, while flush beams fit inside the ceiling for an unbroken plane but require cutting and rehanging ceiling joists.
